nodes.description: Foundational paradigm based on objects containing data and methods

nodes.description: Blueprint or template for creating objects, defining structure and behavior

nodes.label: Encapsulation
nodes.description: Bundling of data and methods together while hiding implementation details

nodes.label: Inheritance
nodes.description: Mechanism allowing classes to inherit properties and methods from parent classes

nodes.label: Polymorphism
nodes.description: Ability of objects to take multiple forms or behave differently based on context

nodes.label: Abstraction
nodes.description: Hiding complexity by showing only necessary features

nodes.label: Composition over Inheritance
nodes.description: Using object composition instead of inheritance for greater flexibility

nodes.label: Design Patterns
nodes.description: Reusable solutions to common problems in object-oriented design

nodes.label: Object/Instance
nodes.description: Runtime instance of a class containing actual data and state

key_insights.insight_1: Class Definition is the central pillar - it enables all other OOP mechanisms
key_insights.insight_2: Encapsulation and Abstraction are complementary: encapsulation protects, abstraction simplifies
key_insights.insight_3: Inheritance and Composition are not competing but complementary patterns with different trade-offs
key_insights.insight_4: Design Patterns are language-agnostic solutions that apply OOP principles
key_insights.insight_5: Polymorphism emerges from proper Inheritance and Abstraction design
key_insights.insight_6: Objects are the runtime manifestation of Classes with encapsulated state
